data.name: Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd
data.about: Dixon Technologies (India) Limited,  incorporated  in  1993 ,  is  a  Electronic  Manufacturing  Services  (EMS)  company  with operations in the electronic products vertical such as consumer electronics, lighting, home appliance, closed-circuit television cameras  (CCTVs), and mobile  phones. It also  undertakes reverse logistics operations.  Besides, it manufactures security surveillance equipment, wearables & audibles, AC-PCBs. Recently, it has entered a JV with Imagine Marketing Private Limited for designing and manufacturing wireless audio solutions in India.[1]

data.what_it_does: Dixon Technologies (India) Limited is a manufacturing services company that produces a wide range of electronics and appliances for domestic and international OEM and ODM customers. Its business spans mobile phones, consumer electronics, home appliances, lighting, and telecom/networking hardware, serving both Indian and global brands.

bull.text: The company delivered a 3-year revenue CAGR of 58.9% and PAT CAGR of 86.1% with a ROCE of 29% and low leverage (debt/equity 0.21).

Management targets camera module revenue to grow from INR 1,700 Cr to INR 2,500 Cr, telecom networking from INR 5,000 Cr to INR 7,500-8,000 Cr, and lighting to double to INR 1,700 Cr after the Signify JV.
Operating cash flow covered PAT 1.08x over three years and the company has filed component scheme applications with ~INR 3,000 Cr investment over three years for backward integration.

bear.text: Operating margin has fallen from 4.3% to 3.8% over three years and the mobile phone segment margin is guided at only 2.8-3.2%, indicating structurally low profitability.
Quarterly revenue is volatile, swinging from INR 14,855 Cr (Sep 2025) to INR 10,511 Cr (Mar 2026) before rebounding to INR 15,548 Cr (Jun 2026).

Most forward guidance remains undelivered: the 4-4.5% margin target was only partly met at 3.8%, while double-digit margin and revenue targets for new businesses are still 'in progress' or 'cannot be checked'.
